analysis.title: GS flow and positioning observations (Sean Vogel, 4 Nov 2026)
key_insights: EMEA head of 1D trading Richard Privorotsky says equity futures dipped sharply overnight and then recovered once the midterm legislative margins and key regional races were decided. He expects vol to struggle to hold a bid and the initial selloff to be absorbed, because many hedges were put on in recent days and now need to be monetized.

Privorotsky says multiples across AI infrastructure have already been aggressively de-rated in anticipation of power and permitting concerns, and he asks how much is already in the price. His gut is that AI infrastructure has been 'sold to death'.

On land and power, the debate has shifted from the cost of compute to whether capacity can be permitted, energized and delivered in 2027-2029. Moratoriums, local opposition to data centers and tighter regulation could constrain supply.

Implication one: suppliers of chips, cooling, electrical equipment and data center hardware risk customers having over-ordered relative to the capacity they can energize. Some demand could move to other geographies or behind-the-meter power, but possibly not fast enough. Much of this risk already appears in multiples.

Implication two: if new supply cannot be delivered, existing energized compute becomes scarcer and more valuable. This potentially benefits hyperscalers and owners of deployed capacity. Neoclouds differ, since some own compute and contracted demand while others depend on new facilities, financing and power delivery.

On the 2027 vs 2029 policy horizon, uncertainty over corporate tax, antitrust/M&A and oversight can cap terminal multiples. The desk counters that with current administration leadership through 2028, companies have an incentive to pull forward capital deployment, permitting and deals into 2027. Historically the S&P 500 has been higher 12 months after all 19 midterm cycles since 1950.

Geopolitics: mediators are still exchanging proposals and the two sides remain far apart, though a limited deal is possible. Trilateral Russia/Ukraine/US talks are scheduled in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11. The desk says another weekend of escalation is equally possible.

AMD reported revenue +45% YoY to $13.4bn and data center +97% to $8.5bn, with Q4 guidance implying another 27% sequential acceleration. Privorotsky calls it the micro evidence the AI trade needed and says it is hard to reconcile with the multiple compression across AI.
Privorotsky reads Intel as a supply, execution and profitability story and not a demand warning, since Intel's data center business grew 78% YoY.

US sales trading (Ariana Contessa): S&P closed +37bps at 7,568 with a $2.3bn market-on-close imbalance to sell. Tech led the bounce, and rate-sensitive pockets lagged as the 10Y rose to 4.96% after a JOLTS beat (7.523M vs est. 7.164M).

Floor activity was a 4 on a 1-10 scale, with asset manager and hedge fund skews roughly flat. The desk saw a more balanced two-way market, with some Semis/AI supply now met by buy tickets after several sessions where supply met almost no defense. Meta and Oracle traded well after recent capital raises.

After the bell: ANET +6% on 3Q growth accelerating to +59% y/y. AMD +7% on better-than-feared revenue and gross margins. PCOR +13% on 3Q revenue of $402mn (+19% y/y vs guide of $382-384mn) and cRPO +29% y/y. BKNG -7% after guiding to a sharp y/y deceleration in 4Q room nights.

Derivatives: skew was smashed in gamma tenors in SPX and NDX. NDX skew steepened in the belly and back-end while SPX flattened throughout. NDX vol was bid on the spot outperformance, and SPX fixed-strike vols were offered into the close as spot faded.

Clients are swapping medium-term vol expressions for owning gamma in both index and single names. The desk saw memory hedges unwound and memory/semis upside bought, and a GS customer sold 10k WDC 15Jan27 300 puts.
The S&P implied move through tomorrow is 1.14%, versus 1.68% for the remainder of the week including tomorrow.

tension_points.bull_case: Existing energized compute becomes scarcer, so pricing could rise for longer for hyperscalers and owners of deployed capacity. AMD's accelerating growth is hard to square with the multiple compression.
tension_points.bear_case: Moratoriums, local opposition and restrictive regulation could limit data center supply, and customers of chip, cooling and electrical suppliers may have over-ordered relative to capacity they can energize.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Geopolitical escalation, such as another weekend of escalation, is named as the swing factor that could move markets quickly in either direction.
